alert_summary: A highly suspicious PowerShell command was detected attempting to delete critical application files, indicating a potential ransomware or destructive attack.

risk_assessment.rationale: The encoded PowerShell command suggests deliberate sabotage of important directories using known malicious techniques. The presence of multiple failed authentication attempts and the use of obfuscated scripts align with common brute-force and evasion tactics seen in high-severity incidents. This combination raises confidence that an active threat is attempting to compromise critical systems.

recommended_actions: Isolate the affected host from the network pending investigation
Review authentication logs for this account over a wider time window
Verify whether the source IP/user is a known, expected service account or automation
Run an antivirus/EDR scan on the affected host
Preserve logs and evidence for the affected host pending further investigation
Escalate to the incident response / Tier 2 team
Notify the asset owner of the affected host or agent
Review firewall/network segmentation rules for the affected subnet
Correlate this indicator against the wider environment beyond this alert's time window
Terminate the suspicious process on the affected host
Review the parent-child process execution tree for the affected host
Manually review the decoded command payload for malicious intent
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Immediately isolate the affected endpoint and any connected systems to prevent lateral movement.
Conduct an in-depth forensic review of all PowerShell execution logs, including those from scheduled tasks or service accounts that may have been compromised.
Block and investigate any network traffic originating from or targeting suspicious domains identified during enrichment (e.g., victimcorp.com, example.com) to confirm exfiltration attempts.
Review and restrict permissions on critical directories such as .dist to ensure only authorized users can modify them.
Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools with behavioral analytics focused on PowerShell obfuscation patterns for real-time alerts.
triage_rationale_experimental: The combination of an encoded malicious command, known MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and high-confidence evidence strongly indicates this is a genuine attack attempt rather than noise or benign activity.
